discussionQuestions: Which of the three areas — armor, fruit, or gifts — do you focus on most?
Which area do you tend to neglect?
Can someone have spiritual gifts without spiritual maturity?
How do the armor, fruit, and gifts work together in the life of a believer?
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Armor of God | Fruit of the Spirit | Gifts of the Spirit
Key Scriptures
 Armor of God: Ephesians 6:10-18
 Fruit of the Spirit: Galatians 5:22-23
 Gifts of the Spirit: 1 Corinthians 12:7-11

sections.heading: THE ARMOR OF GOD
sections.body:
Purpose: To Stand
Key Verse: Ephesians 6:11
"Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil."

Armor - Reference

Belt of Truth - Ephesians 6:14
Breastplate of Righteousness - Ephesians 6:14
Shoes of the Gospel of Peace - Ephesians 6:15
Shield of Faith - Ephesians 6:16 - Helmet of Salvation - Ephesians 6:17
Sword of the Spirit - Ephesians 6:17

sections.heading: THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT
sections.body:
Purpose: To Become Like Christ
Key Verse: Galatians 5:22-23
"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace..."

Fruit - Reference

Love - Galatians 5:22
Joy - Galatians 5:22
Peace - Galatians 5:22
Patience - Galatians 5:22
Kindness - Galatians 5:22
Goodness - Galatians 5:22
Faithfulness - Galatians 5:22
Gentleness - Galatians 5:23
Self-Control - Galatians 5:23

sections.heading: THE GIFTS OF THE SPIRIT
sections.body:
Purpose: To Serve Others
Key Verse: 1 Corinthians 12:7
"The manifestation of the Spirit is given to each one for the profit of all."
Gift
Reference
Word of Wisdom - 1 Corinthians 12:8
Word of Knowledge - 1 Corinthians 12:8
Faith - 1 Corinthians 12:9
Gifts of Healing - 1 Corinthians 12:9
Working of Miracles - 1 Corinthians 12:10
Prophecy - 1 Corinthians 12:10
Discerning of Spirits - 1 Corinthians 12:10
Different Kinds of Tongues - 1 Corinthians 12:10
Interpretation of Tongues - 1 Corinthians 12:10

sections.heading: Functional Aspects of the Fruit and Gifts of the Holy Spirit
sections.body:
The Holy Spirit works in two complementary ways. The Fruit of the Spirit produces spiritual character through internal transformation, helping believers become like Christ (Galatians 5:22–23). The Gifts of the Spirit empower believers for outward ministry, enabling them to serve others effectively and bring edification to the Body of Christ (1 Corinthians 12:7–11).

Fruit: "Who am I becoming?" → Become like Christ; Maturity (Galatians 5:22–23).

Gifts: "How can I serve?" → Serve others effectively; Edification of the Body of Christ (1 Corinthians 12:7–11).

Fruit benefits the believer; gifts benefit the Body of Christ and those around the believer (Galatians 5:22–23; 1 Corinthians 12:7–11).

sections.heading: A PRACTICAL COMPARISON
sections.body:
Imagine a Soldier
Armor of God - The soldier's equipment. Without armor, he becomes vulnerable.
Fruit of the Spirit - The soldier's character. Without character, he becomes unstable.
Gifts of the Spirit - The soldier's abilities and assignments. Without gifts, he becomes ineffective.
Armor protects him.
Fruit shapes him.
Gifts use him.

sections.heading: CONCLUSION
sections.body:
Many Christians focus on one area while neglecting the others. God desires believers to be:
 Protected through the Armor of God
 Transformed through the Fruit of the Spirit
 Empowered through the Gifts of the Spirit
A mature believer should possess all three.

sections.heading: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
sections.body:
1. Which of the three areas do you focus on most?
2. Which area do you tend to neglect?
3. Can someone have spiritual gifts without spiritual maturity?
4. How do the Armor, Fruit, and Gifts work together in the life of a believer?
Closing Thought

The Armor of God helps us stand.
The Fruit of the Spirit helps us grow.
The Gifts of the Spirit help us serve.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the armor of God?
quiz.explanation: Ephesians 6:11 — to stand against the wiles of the devil.

quiz.question: What is the fruit of the Spirit meant to produce?
Why are spiritual gifts given according to 1 Corinthians 12:7?
quiz.explanation: Gifts build up the body of Christ.

quiz.question: In the soldier analogy, what does the fruit of the Spirit represent?
quiz.explanation: Fruit shapes who the believer is becoming.

quiz.question: What does a mature believer need according to this study?
options: Only one of the three areas
quiz.explanation: God desires believers who are protected, transformed, and empowered.

title: Armor of God, Fruit of the Spirit, Gifts of the Spirit
description: A Back to the Bible study comparing three essential aspects of the Christian life — standing firm, growing in character, and serving others.

passageReading.text:
10 Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.
11 Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
12 For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.
13 Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
